Meta.content:
# How to write prompts that get great answers from Llama

Tell Llama the job, the material, the reader and the shape of the result. Here is a method you can reuse for any task, with side-by-side examples and follow-ups that fix weak drafts.

Advertisement

Llama answers from only two things: what it learned in training and what you put in your message. It cannot look anything up, it does not know your situation, and it does not remember your other conversations. So the quality of the answer depends heavily on the quality of the request. The good news is that writing a strong prompt is a skill you can learn in an afternoon. This guide gives you a four-question method, side-by-side examples and the follow-up moves that rescue weak drafts.

## Answer four questions before you press send

Think of Llama as a capable new colleague on their first day: quick and well read, but knowing nothing about your project. Before you write, answer these four questions in the prompt itself.

- What is the job? Start with an action verb: draft, shorten, explain, compare, list, fix, translate, plan. One clear job per message works best.
- What should it work from? Paste the text, the numbers, the error message or your notes. Without material, Llama fills the gaps with guesses that only sound right.
- Who is it for? A teacher, a customer, a ten-year-old, your manager, yourself. The reader decides vocabulary, depth and tone.
- What shape should the result take? A table, a checklist, three options, an email under 120 words, code only with no explanation.

A simple question needs only the first point: "What is the capital of Peru?" is a perfectly good prompt. A message to a client, a study plan or a product page needs all four.

## Weak and strong prompts, side by side

### Planning a trip
Weak:
Plan a trip to Lisbon.
Strong:
Plan 3 days in Lisbon for two adults in early spring. We like food
markets, viewpoints and walking; we don't enjoy museums. Moderate
budget. Give one table per day with morning, afternoon and evening,
and a short note on getting between places on foot or by tram.

The first version gets you a brochure. The second gets a plan built around your interests, in a layout you can scan on your phone. Llama cannot check today's opening hours or ticket prices, though: it has no internet access and its knowledge stops at a cut-off date. Confirm those details yourself before you go.

### Summarising something you paste
Weak:
summarize this [long report pasted below]
Strong:
Summarize the report below for a busy manager who has two minutes.
Give: 1) the main finding in one sentence, 2) three supporting points,
3) any risks or open questions the report mentions. Use only what is
in the text. If something is unclear, say so instead of guessing.

"""
[paste the report here]
"""

Putting the instructions first and the material between triple quotes keeps the two apart. The line "use only what is in the text" makes invented details less likely.

### Writing for customers
Weak:
Write a product description for my candle.
Strong:
Write a product description for a handmade soy candle: 200 g, scent
fig and cedar, sold in a reusable ceramic cup. Audience: people buying
a gift online. Tone: warm, not cheesy. Give me 3 versions: about 30
words, about 80 words and about 150 words.

The colleague test: read your prompt as if someone had sent it to you. If you would need to ask a question before starting, put the answer into the prompt now.

Advertisement

## Prompts for images with Llama 4

Both Llama 4 models in our chat, Maverick and Scout, can read a picture you attach: a photo of a whiteboard, a chart, a menu in another language, a screenshot of an error. You can add one image per message. The same rule applies as with text: say exactly what you want done with the image.
Weak:
[photo] what is this
Strong:
[photo of a handwritten shopping list] Type this list out as plain
text, grouped by supermarket section. Mark any word you cannot read
with (?) instead of guessing.

Asking Llama to flag what it cannot read matters, because models sometimes "read" blurry text by guessing. Llama 3.3 70B and Llama 3.1 8B are text-only; if you attach an image while one of them is selected, the chat switches to Llama 4 Maverick. Our guide on choosing the right Llama model explains the differences.

## Five patterns worth knowing

### Give it a standard to meet

Instead of "act as an expert", say which standard the expert would apply: "Review this cover letter the way a recruiter scanning fifty applications would, and point out anything that would make you stop reading." A role helps only when it changes what the model pays attention to.

### Show, don't describe

Words like "professional" or "fun" mean different things to different people. Paste two or three lines you like and write "match the rhythm and vocabulary of these examples". Llama copies a pattern far more reliably than it follows an adjective.

### Ask it to interview you first

For bigger tasks, end with: "Before you write anything, ask me up to five questions." You get a better first draft, and you notice what you forgot to mention. Try the interview-me prompt in the chat.

### Ask for options, then choose

"Give me six headline ideas in different styles" is faster than rejecting one headline six times. Pick the best one and ask for variations on it.

### Ask for steps on hard problems

For maths, logic and debugging, add "work through it step by step, then give the final answer on its own line". You can then check each step instead of trusting a single number at the end.

Advertisement

## Steer with follow-ups instead of starting over

The chat remembers the conversation you are in, so the second message is often where the real work happens. Follow-ups that fix most drafts:

- "Cut this by half. Keep the facts, drop the warm-up sentences."
- "Paragraph two is right. Rewrite the others to match its tone."
- "You assumed I have a car. I don't, so redo the plan."
- "List the assumptions you made so I can correct them."
- "Turn this into a table with columns for option, cost and effort."

In our chat you can also edit an earlier message and resend it, or regenerate an answer and switch between versions. Editing is better than piling on corrections when the first prompt was off from the start. When a long conversation starts going in circles or forgetting what you said at the beginning, start fresh: ask Llama to sum up the key decisions so far, then paste that recap into a new chat. Very long conversations are trimmed before they reach the model.

## Small adjustments for each model

- Llama 3.1 8B is the smallest model in our chat. Give it one clear task at a time and simple formats. It suits quick rewrites, short answers and brainstorming.
- Llama 3.3 70B is a strong text-only all-rounder. Numbered requirements help it cover every point you asked for.
- Llama 4 Maverick (the default) and Llama 4 Scout also take images. Name what you want from the image in the same message.

Whatever the model, write in the language you want back. According to Meta's model cards, Llama 4 officially supports 12 languages and Llama 3.3 and 3.1 support 8. Other languages often work too, with more mistakes.

## Common traps

- Asking about recent events. Llama has no web access. For news, prices, timetables or anything after its cut-off, use a current source.
- Leading questions. "Why is plan A better?" invites agreement. Ask "Compare plan A and plan B, including the weaknesses of each" instead.
- Several unrelated tasks in one message. Split them up, or number them clearly.
- Sharing more than needed. Replace names, addresses and account numbers with placeholders such as [CLIENT]. Our privacy and safety guide explains why.
- Treating confident answers as checked facts. Fluent is not the same as correct; see how to fact-check AI answers.

You do not have to start from a blank box. Our prompt library collects ready-made prompts with blanks to complete, sorted into writing, study, business and everyday life, and the AI tools build a structured prompt for you behind the scenes.

Advertisement

## FAQ

### Is there a perfect prompt formula?

No. The four questions (job, material, reader, shape) cover most cases, but the best prompt is the one that gives Llama the details only you know. Clear beats clever.

### Does my prompt have to be in English?

Not at all. Llama is instructed to answer in whatever language you write in, so use the one you want back. If you want a different language, say so, for example "Answer in Portuguese".

### Why does the same prompt give different answers?

Language models choose each next word with some randomness, so the wording changes from run to run. Regenerate a few times and keep the best version. Our guide to how large language models work explains why.

### Can Llama remember my preferences between chats?

No. Each conversation starts fresh. Your history is saved in your browser so you can reopen old chats, but a new chat knows nothing about them. Paste your standing preferences at the start, or pick one of the assistants, which come with instructions already set.

### How long can a prompt be?

Long enough to include what matters; a few paragraphs of context is normal. For very long documents, send them in parts and ask for a summary of each part, because the chat limits how much text goes into a single request.

## Ask Llama your first question

No account and nothing to install. Open the chat, type a message and see what Llama can do.
Open Llama chat

Meta.content:
# AI Code Assistant

Paste code or describe what it should do, choose a task and a language, and get working code in formatted blocks with a short explanation.

Advertisement

## What the Code Assistant does

The Code Assistant is a quick programming helper in your browser. Describe a function and get working code, paste a snippet and an error message to find the bug, or ask what an unfamiliar piece of code does. It can also review code for problems, write unit tests and add comments. Code comes back in formatted blocks with syntax highlighting, ready to copy.

It runs on Llama 4 Maverick, Meta's open-weight model, which Meta describes as producing multilingual text and code. We reach it through a cloud inference provider. The tool is told to name the cause of a bug before fixing it, to avoid inventing library functions, and to say what you should check when the answer depends on versions or code it cannot see.

## How to use it

- Paste code or describe the task. Include the error message and what you expected to happen. For new code, list inputs, outputs and any constraints.
- Choose the task: write code, find and fix bugs, explain code, review and improve, write tests, or add comments.
- Choose the language, or leave it on "Detect automatically". The list includes Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, C#, C++, C, PHP, Go, Rust, Kotlin, Swift, Ruby, SQL, Bash and HTML with CSS.
- Press Generate (or Ctrl+Enter). Copy the code from the result, Regenerate for another approach, or Continue in chat to iterate on it.

Advertisement

## Tips for useful answers

- Paste the full error. The exact message and the line it points to say more than "it doesn't work".
- Keep snippets focused. Paste the function that fails and the code that calls it, not the whole project. Remove keys, passwords and private data first.
- Mention versions. "Python 3.12", "React 18" or "PostgreSQL 16" helps avoid answers written for an older API.
- Ask for explanations at your level. In the chat, add "I am a beginner" or "skip the basics" to change the depth.
- Iterate in the chat. After the first answer, Continue in chat and ask for edge cases, better names or a version without a library.

## Example

Request: Why do I get "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'price')"?
function total(items) {
  let sum = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i <= items.length; i++) {
    sum += items[i].price;
  }
  return sum;
}
Answer (shortened): The loop runs one step too far. Array indexes go from 0 to
items.length - 1, but the condition i <= items.length also runs the loop when i equals the length. At that point items[i] is undefined, and reading .price from it throws the error. Change the condition to i < items.length, or use items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price, 0).

## Limits and safe use

- Test before you ship. Generated code can look right and still fail on edge cases. Run it, read it and add tests.
- It cannot run your code. The tool does not execute anything or see your files. It reasons from the text you paste.
- Knowledge has a cut-off. Meta gives August 2024 as the cut-off of the training data. Newer libraries or API changes may be missing, so check the official documentation.
- Security matters. Review generated code for injection risks, unsafe input handling and secrets in the code before using it in production.
- Licenses. If you reuse code in a commercial project, make sure it does not reproduce someone else's licensed code.

Advertisement

## FAQ

### Is the Code Assistant free?

Yes, with no account. Each request uses one message from your free daily allowance, shared with the chat and the other tools and reset daily.

### Which programming languages does it support?

The menu lists 16 common languages plus automatic detection. Others, such as Dart, Scala or Lua, often work too if you name them in your request.

### Can I paste a whole project?

No. The box takes a few thousand characters. Paste the relevant files or functions. In the chat you can choose Llama 4 Scout, the model with the longest context, for bigger pieces of code.

### Can I explain code in my own language?

Yes. Write your request in your language and the explanation follows it, while the code itself stays in the programming language.

### Where can I learn to use AI for programming?

Read our guide on AI for coding, or start a debugging prompt in the chat. For math behind an algorithm, try the Math Solver.

## Ask Llama your first question

No account and nothing to install. Open the chat, type a message and see what Llama can do.
Open Llama chat

GLM.content:
# 智谱下一代参数1.6万亿是烟雾弹？发布即服务要掀桌子！

先交代一下，专家纪要这东西，是投资机构通过专家网络平台约谈产业人士形成的记录，通常按小时计费，受访者多为在职或离业的行业内人员，不代表公司官方口径，但经常会有意外收获。这份智谱的纪要真假自行判断，不过信息量确实可观。你把它当“路边社”也行，但当“路边社”把细节说得比官宣还细的时候，你就得多看两眼了。

我把这份纪要归纳成四本账，一本一本翻。

第一本账：参数账——市场给安排的是“追平”，纪要爆料的是“跨代”。

10月底发新模型、参数1.6万亿，这个传闻在市场上传了一个月。本次纪要给出了另一个版本：传闻不实，新一代基座模型实际参数规模在2.5万亿到3.5万亿之间。你品品这个差距。1.6万亿是什么水平？DeepSeek V4 Pro公开报道口径是1.6万亿总参，此前有传闻美团在做1.6万亿，Kimi K3也在万亿档。也就是说，市场给GLM下一代安排的参数量，只是追平国内第一梯队的现有水位。而纪要里的2.5到3.5万亿，直接越过这一档，接近3万亿的中位数意味着规模翻倍再翻倍。这个数字指向的是唐杰10月初新加坡演讲里说的目标：预训练数据和规模扩到数万亿token级，参数从当前约7400亿上探1万亿以上。专家纪要的数字比演讲口径还要激进一倍以上，真实性留给发布日检验，但方向是一致的——下一代GLM的第一关键词是规模跃迁。市场给它安排的是“追上前面那辆车”，纪要爆料的是“直接换赛道”；追平是竞争，跨代是重排。

第二本账：架构账——训推一体，发布首日就要大规模服务，这是要掀行业惯例的桌子。

纪要还透露了两个此前没有公开过的细节。其一，架构激进，目标是训得快、推得快、压低推理端成本，发布第一天就能大规模服务。这四个目标同时成立非常难，大参数模型的历史包袱恰恰是“发得出、供不上”，发布初期限流几乎是行业惯例。把推理效率写进基座设计的硬约束，意味着这次不是训完再优化推理，是训练和推理一起设计。其二，为支撑这个方案，智谱补强了infra团队。结合此前10万卡集群、吞吐3.2倍的公开成果，infra这条线在下一代模型里的权重只会更高。

你想想“发布首日大规模服务”这句话的分量。此前旗舰模型的收入曲线是梯形的：发布、限流、扩容、放量，爬坡以月计。首日即可大规模服务意味着曲线变成阶跃的，发布即峰值供给。行业惯例是“先发再扩”，它要的是“发即扩”；梯形爬坡是慢慢收钱，阶跃供给是发布日就开收。 这不是技术升级，这是商业节奏的升级。

第三本账：时间账——延期是因为loss不降，这个坦诚反而增加了可信度。

发布时间的悬念也给了答案：纪要说是比市场预期晚，是因为基座训练一度出现loss不降。这个坦诚的细节反而增加了可信度，超大参数训练踩坑确实是常态。近期问题已解决，预计很快完成训练，下一代的目标水位是Fable级旗舰。你品品，如果纪要只吹“我们特别强、马上发”，你反而要打个问号；它说“我们踩坑了、loss不降、延期了、现在解决了”，这反而像真话。吹牛的人只说结果，干活的人会说过程；loss不降这种事敢说出来，比一百句“进展顺利”都值钱。

第四本账：商业账——云厂商发布前就谈分成，渠道比产品先就位。

### They seized influence through technical skill. Now they must use it to protect the freedom that produced it.

Four months before Kimi planned to release K3, its flagship model, young researchers asked Moonshot’s CEO Yang Zhilin to change its architecture. For two decades, power at China’s internet companies followed commercial success: Build a hit product, win a market, make more money—and gain more influence. Now technologists in their late 20s and early 30s are taking control of R&D decisions before their products have proved commercially successful.

Yang, 33, has made Alibaba and Tencent both rivals and investors in Moonshot AI. At Xiaomi, 31-year-old Luo Fuli leads a team of dozens training a trillion-parameter model. At Tencent, 28-year-old Yao Shunyu joined the office of the president and took over Hunyuan.

Their choices direct hundreds of researchers and enormous computing resources. In September, Luo showed Xiaomi’s training dashboards for two models; the displayed rates put their combined cost at $30,800 an hour.

These leaders are building teams with fewer management layers and more freedom to test ideas. As one tech lead at an AI model company told us: “Hire talented people and give them GPUs.” Their power rests not only on technical skill, but on the ability to spot promising ideas, direct scarce resources and persuade an organization to take a bet. How they do so will help shape China’s increasingly expensive AI race.

## China’s Young AI Leaders Decide How Its Top Labs Deploy Their Most Valuable Resources

### At Kimi, Yang Zhilin Chooses to Wait

In March 2026, several young researchers at Kimi wanted the company to alter the plan for K3, its next flagship model, just four months before its expected release. Their proposal, Attention Residuals, could improve the model’s training efficiency. But changing the architecture so late could delay training and the launch. Before thousands of GPUs began running, they needed CEO Yang Zhilin’s approval.

The idea came from Su Jianlin, a Kimi researcher known to peers as “God Su（苏神）.” He lives in Guangzhou and works remotely with Kimi’s Beijing team. For years, he had written about mathematics and model research on his blog, attracting readers who later became his colleagues.

Around the Lunar New Year, Su read a DeepSeek paper on ways to improve how a large language model moves information between its layers. His idea was simple: apply Attention—a technique models use to determine which parts of an input matter most—not just to text tokens but across layers. That would let each layer choose which information to draw from earlier ones.

Su quickly built a prototype. Zhang Yu, a young doctoral researcher, and Chen Guangyu, then a 17-year-old high school student, joined him to test it on bigger models. Zhang had studied efficient model designs during his Ph.D. at Soochow University and later became the first author of Kimi’s Linear paper. Chen, despite still being in high school, had also spent years on the same problem. More complicated versions mostly performed worse than the first, simpler one.

The problem was cost. The full design required the model to retain information from every layer and move it between devices. The inference team thought it could be optimized, but the training team concluded Kimi did not have enough computing resources. “Put simply, we couldn’t afford it,” Su later wrote.

Kimi’s traffic was also growing quickly, putting pressure on the company to reduce both response times and inference costs. Its infrastructure team asked for a design that would keep related data closer together, reducing the information that had to move between devices. Zhang and Chen came up with a block-based version in a single night. Rather than retain every layer’s information, it grouped layers and applied Attention between the groups. It added no more than 5% in overhead, according to the paper and the team’s review data, while improving training efficiency by about 20%.

The work was possible because Kimi’s algorithm and infrastructure teams trusted each other’s constraints. Yaoyu Wang, an AI infrastructure engineer, later described an internal meme: infrastructure engineers say a mathematically sound design should be buildable; algorithm researchers reply that if it is not, the algorithm has not been thought through.

Once Kimi’s training, inference and infrastructure teams agreed the design could work, the company pushed to add it to K3. Yet K3 was about to begin training, and the new architecture still needed testing. Yang agreed to delay the start of training, giving the team time to validate it.

发布于：北京市

（来源：机器之心）

机器之心编辑部

大的要来了，而且一下来了俩。

最近两天，人们在 Arena.ai（原 LMArena）的编程对战 Code Arena 中发现了两个陌生的名字：Kibitz、Kalmia。厂商在正式发布前，经常会把新模型以匿名代号放进盲测，让真实用户在不知情的情况下投票。经过仔细分析，很多人把它们与国产新模型联系在了一块。人们认为 Kibitz 疑似是月之暗面的 Kimi K3.1，Kalmia 疑似阿里的 Qwen 4。

先来看看效果，X 上有人不停「抽卡」，用刷到的新模型制作出了不少 SVG、网页和可交互的 3D 场景。

「build what you think you look like in Minecraft」：

Kibitz 构建的中世纪像素城堡：

Kalmia 构建的 3D 可驾驶汽车：

Kibitz 与 Kalmia 构建的直升机：

AI 构建这些效果需要协调场景绘制、运动、镜头和用户输入，相当于一次性完成前端开发、空间建模与交互逻辑，这为我们观察模型的前端开发、空间表达和指令遵循能力提供了直观的窗口。

大家对于这两个模型能够实现的效果表示惊叹，认为 Kibitz 或许可以创下开源模型的新高，而 Kalmia 甚至能够比肩 GPT 6.1 Sol Ultra。

同样让人在意的是成本，Arena 能查看部分费用指标，社区有人表示，Kibitz 做同样的事，Token 成本只是 GPT‑6 Astra 的 1/14。

有关两家的新模型，Kimi K 3.1 即将发布的消息比较有谱。前天在 AI 社区已有人公布了一次对 Kimi 官方域名下配置接口的请求，返回内容包含切换目标 "to": "k3.1" 等，这说明产品端已经在准备 K3.1 的会话切换。不过，发帖者随后更新称，该配置当晚已被撤回。

另一条线索来自模型处理特殊字符串时留下的「指纹」。

AI Tracker Bot 表示，在两次测试中，Kibitz 对 11 个用于识别 Moonshot 模型的特殊 token 都出现了乱码，与该账号测试过的 Kimi 模型表现一致，而来自其他 7 家 AI 实验室的模型则能够准确复制这些内容。这让 Kibitz 与 Kimi 的联系进一步加强。

有关 Qwen 4，我们目前比较清楚的是它的技术方向。

在 8 月份发布 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 的时候，新模型在官方模型卡中被明确定位为 Qwen 4 底层架构的实验预览。它引入了结合 Gated DeltaNet 与 Qwen Sparse Attention 的混合注意力、门控残差连接，以及 N-gram Embedding，分别探索长上下文处理、跨层信息传递与参数扩展的效率。

其中，Qwen Sparse Attention 以小块为单位选择需要处理的内容，旨在降低长上下文延迟；N-gram Embedding 则利用短词元序列进行索引，为模型扩展参数提供计算开销较低、便于卸载存储的路径。这意味着 Qwen 4 已有公开的架构探索作为铺垫。不过现在仅看匿名测试，我们肯定无法确定它采用了哪些具体设计。

通常，匿名上 Arena 是新模型发布的最后一环：Kimi K3 发布前，代号 Kivine 的模型提前数天现身；而 Qwen3.8-Max 发布前，代号 Kaleb 仅仅提前一天出现。

# SpaceX Is Working With Nvidia, Apollo And Other Top Tech And Consulting Firms On A Grok Partnership Program

## SpaceX has launched a formal program backed by over 130 technology, consulting, and finance leaders to scale Grok AI and agentic software development.

- SpaceX launched the Super Intelligence Partner Network with more than 130 early-access companies, including Nvidia, Apollo, Snowflake, Databricks, and Bain & Co.
- The initiative categorizes participants into Transformation Partners—who assist clients in integrating Grok into complex operations—and Marketplace Partners, who develop specialized software integrations.
- The launch follows strong financial performance from SpaceX’s AI division and a doubling of weekly active Grok Bot enterprise users to over 800,000 in October.

SpaceX (SPCX) on Thursday announced the launch of its official SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network, which aims to help businesses build, integrate, and scale applications using the company’s Grok AI platform.

The network debuts with more than 130 inaugural participants from the technology, financial, and management consulting sectors. Notable launch partners include Nvidia Corp.(NVDA), Apollo Global Management, Snowflake Inc., Databricks Inc., and Bain & Co.

SPCX stock dropped about 7% on Thursday as investors judge the timeline of a possible SpaceX-Tesla merger.

## SpaceX’s Strategic Network

The Super Intelligence Partner Network categorizes participating organizations into two main operating tiers: Transformation Partners and Marketplace Partners.

Transformation Partners focus on enterprise-wide implementations. These organizations help clients deploy Grok to restructure internal operations, relying in part on a specialized "Forward Deployed Engineer" accreditation program. Participating firms, such as AI services provider Galatiq, send engineers directly into client environments to embed autonomous workflows into everyday operations.

Marketplace Partners are tasked with building software integrations and extensions. These connectors allow Grok and its underlying development tools—including the recently acquired Cursor AI coding platform—to link into established corporate databases, communications tools, and security architecture.

## Expanding Beyond Experimental Use

SpaceX executives highlighted a shift among enterprise clients away from simple AI experimentation toward full-scale autonomous workflows.

SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell noted during a recent earnings call that weekly paid users for Grok Bot climbed to more than 800,000 as of October, double the previous month’s figure. Shotwell described the agentic software as an "always-on teammate" deployed across software engineering, sales, marketing, and IT operations.

"We're seeing a fundamental shift from AI-assisted to AI-led software development," said Chuck Whitten, global head of Bain & Company’s Applied Technology & AI Practice. Whitten emphasized that integrating AI deeply into the software development lifecycle represents a strategic imperative for C-suite leaders aiming to boost productivity and execution speed.

## Ecosystem Synergy And Enterprise Guardrails

The launch underscores deeper cross-industry ties among firms in Elon Musk's corporate ecosystem. Nvidia VP of Strategic Enterprise Partnerships Pat Lee noted that Cursor is deployed across Nvidia’s engineering group, while asset manager Apollo Global Management was an early internal tester of Grok following financing deals for SpaceX’s AI computing infrastructure.

To address corporate concerns surrounding security, privacy, and compliance, partner infrastructure providers are embedding enterprise controls into the platform.

Vivek Raghunathan, senior vice president of engineering at Snowflake, emphasized that an AI agent's utility relies heavily on organizational context and safety. "SpaceX Super Intelligence provides the autonomous workflow builders want, while Snowflake serves as the enterprise AI platform ensuring every action adheres to organizational logic, system guardrails, and strict audit trails," Raghunathan said.

新計劃名為SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network，參與企業還包括Bain \& Co\.、Booz Allen Hamilton及AI工程服務商Galatiq。

馬斯克亦表示，Grok Bot已在部分企業客戶進行早期部署，預計未來數星期擴大應用範圍。

\#\# AI部門首次錄得盈利 SpaceX加快尋找企業客戶

SpaceX本周公布第三季業績，旗下Super Intelligence業務錄得盈利，但主要受惠於孟菲斯數據中心的算力租賃合約，而非Grok軟件銷售。

公司此前已收購AI編程工具Cursor，並加強整合Grok及企業服務。今次擴大合作網絡，是將龐大AI算力轉化為企業軟件收入的另一部署。

### 1. OpenAI Decisions API 全面开放，决策模型开打价格战

Mino 评论：注意它没有专门训练一个新模型，只是把 Luna 的推理路径改快、改便宜——这说明“决策模型”这个品类的护城河暂时不在模型本身，而在延迟与校准。对你们更实际：反欺诈规则命中的那一类“在几个动作里选一个”的链路，天然适合这种 System One 模型。先拿一个离线场景做对照实验，把 200 毫秒当成新的预算线来设计。

### 2. Canva 发布首个自研图像模型 Craft

cross_cutting.description: How 70% to 80% ... now written by AI, why its Friday product meetings show what shipped that week, and why a new product only needs to be 60% to 70% ready at launch ... 6. Launch at 60% to 70% ... is now written by AI ... 60% to 70% ready.
cross_cutting.content:
Two to three years ago, software companies were still planning product roadmaps in years and quarters. Today, as one of our guests put it, the only question that matters is “what are we shipping this week?”

That guest was Chano Fernández, co-CEO of Klaviyo. He joined us to explain how AI agents are reshaping marketing and customer engagement, why taste may be the biggest moat AI companies can build, and what it really takes for a public software company to stay relevant when the ground keeps moving.

Chano held senior leadership roles at SAP before becoming co-CEO of Workday, where he helped expand its global and enterprise business. He was then co-CEO of the AI-native talent platform Eightfold, and spent two years on Klaviyo’s board, most recently as interim executive. In January, he became co-CEO alongside co-founder Andrew Bialecki. Andrew focuses fully on Klaviyo’s AI vision and products, while Chano runs go-to-market, operations, and G&A. Klaviyo now serves more than 200,000 customers, with around 9 billion profiles and 250 billion transactions a quarter on the platform.

Why email may become less relevant as AI agents start reading it for us, and why Klaviyo’s 14 years of data and infrastructure can’t be replicated with vibe coding

Inside Composer, Klaviyo’s agentic marketing tool: seven or eight sub-agents, and why getting a campaign to come out “80% or 90% right” for a CMO comes down to taste

Where software pricing is heading: from seats to consumption to outcome-based deals, and the 5% to 6% revenue share Chano is seeing emerge across the industry

How 70% to 80% of Klaviyo’s code is now written by AI, why its Friday product meetings show what shipped that week, and why a new product only needs to be 60% to 70% ready at launch

How the co-CEO model works in practice: a written operating agreement, two to three calls a day, and why only a handful of decisions each year really need both of them

1. Agents will read your emails for you
Chano thinks email’s role changes once AI agents start acting on our behalf.

“I believe it will become less relevant, just because some of those agents will be the ones consuming many of those emails going forward.”

Email won’t disappear. It will stay one of the cheapest and most efficient channels. Chano also expects agents to do more than read: they will use what they know about us to surface better products, offers and services. For brands, the challenge is personalizing at scale, and that is where automation and agents come in.

2. Marketing and service are becoming one
Moving Klaviyo from a marketing tool to an AI agent platform wasn’t optional.

“The boundaries between marketing and service have become more indistinct.”

If a customer has just complained or asked for a refund, the next thing they want is not a promotion. Most brands can’t see that, because their data sits across six or seven disconnected systems with no real-time view. Chano says this is where Klaviyo’s infrastructure gives it an edge: around 9 billion profiles, 250 billion transactions a quarter, and the ability to send 100 million messages in 20 minutes.

3. Taste is the hardest thing to automate
Klaviyo’s agent, Composer, builds campaign calendars and campaigns for brands that are short on people or ideas. Getting the output right comes down to taste.

“If you’re a chief marketing officer, you want to see the campaign the agent is creating and say: wow, this is really my brand, my image, my language.”

Code is fairly deterministic: good code is good code at any company. Brand voice is different for every customer. Klaviyo measures progress through thumbs-up ratings, how many campaigns go live without edits, and direct customer feedback. Each edit a brand makes feeds the next model.

4. Stay model-agnostic and route by task
With AI labs shipping updates every few weeks, Chano says no company can afford to lock itself to one model.

“It’s important to be as model-agnostic as possible.”

Composer runs on at least seven or eight sub-agents, covering email templates, flow templates and campaign taste, and each can sit on a different underlying model. Klaviyo’s engineers test new releases quickly and change the routing when a better model appears. Chano expects model capabilities to become more standardized, so routing well will matter more than picking a winner.

5. Pricing is heading towards outcomes
Klaviyo had a head start on the shift away from per-seat pricing.

“We were never on seat-based pricing like many other SaaS companies.”

Klaviyo’s pricing has always tracked sends and profiles, rising and falling with seasons like Black Friday. Its customer service agent already charges only when it resolves a conversation. Chano sees the industry settling on a base subscription with usage on top. Outcome-based deals come next, where the vendor takes a share of attributed revenue. The benchmark he is seeing is 5% to 6%.

6. Launch at 60% to 70%
Around 70% to 80% of Klaviyo’s code is now written by AI, and the planning cadence has changed with it.

“Two to three years ago, we were still talking about product roadmaps in years and in quarters, and the conversation today is: what are we shipping this week?”

Every Friday, a group of engineers presents what shipped that week. The hard call is when to launch. Customers have less patience than in the old SaaS era, when a product had 12 to 24 months to mature. AI products can also improve dramatically within weeks. Chano’s threshold is a product that is 60% to 70% ready.

7. Co-CEOs only work with trust, complementary skills and low ego
Chano was on Klaviyo’s board when the company decided Andrew Bialecki needed to spend all his time on product vision.

“It’s not an easy model, but it’s a very effective one.”

The two wrote down how they would run the company and speak two to three times a day. Andrew owns product; Chano owns go-to-market and the rest of the business. At first they held joint one-to-ones with leaders, which are no longer needed. Chano’s view is that only a handful of decisions each year, on strategy, culture and organization, need both of them. The rest can be made by either and reversed if needed.

8. Focus on inputs, not the share price
With Klaviyo’s stock down 35% this year at the time of this recording, Chano says his answer is to focus on what the company controls.

“If you take care of the right inputs, the outputs will take care of themselves.”

For Chano, the inputs are innovation, happy and referenceable customers, the right culture, and getting the few big decisions right. He sees the market as trying to separate AI wrappers from companies with durable moats. In his view, that will get easier as more AI-native companies go public, and it could take anywhere from two to six quarters.
